dedupe_keys.name: nus credit research initiative cri probability of default and credit risk data

description: The Credit Research Initiative publishes probabilities of default for more than 90,000 exchange-listed companies worldwide, with horizons from one month to five years, produced daily with a published, regularly updated method. It also offers aggregate probabilities by country and sector, a Corporate Vulnerability Index, distance-to-default measures, a bottom-up default analysis tool developed with the International Monetary Fund for stress testing, and, since January 2026, a pilot of credit risk data for private small firms. It is a non-profit undertaking of the Asian Institute of Digital Finance at the National University of Singapore, launched in July 2009 at the university's Risk Management Institute. Coverage is global. For non-commercial use the data can be viewed online and downloaded as monthly CSV files after signing in, with historical files lagging one to one and a half years; API access and commercial use are arranged by contacting CRI. Caveats: the measures are model outputs, and CRI states that it is not a licensed or accredited credit rating agency, so they should not be used as ratings. For simulation it gives firm-level default risk that can flag fragile banks, utilities and industrial firms and seed financial contagion and stress scenarios. It is related to the FRED record in this catalogue, which holds macro-financial series often combined with such measures.
